From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps from today — latency/throughput checklist

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking through RetailCo's fraud-detection assistant use case and for sharing the example traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

What we heard
- Peak inference pattern: 350 concurrent users, ~60 requests/s at peak; median prompt length ~70 tokens, responses ~220 tokens (avg generation ~290 tokens).
- Hard SLO: 95% requests under 1800 ms total server-side latency.
- Priority: cost and consistent P95/P99 latency; model quality acceptable within current baseline.

Immediate asks from our side
1) Confirm whether the 60 req/s is steady-state or bursty (e.g., 10s spikes to 200 req/s).
2) If you have a small sample of traces (timestamps + token counts) we can use those to shape batching settings.

What we promised
- Marissa will run a short micro-benchmark against a comparable open model profile for the 290-token generation shape and share P50/P90/P99 + tokens/sec with 1-8 concurrency and batching configs. See attached quick reference.
- I’ll follow up if we haven’t heard back in ~5 business days to check priority/timing and offer a concise PoC plan (2-week sandbox or a single production route pilot).

Attachments: redwood-latency-p99-vs-batch.pdf (small reference chart)
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678/RC-3481

If any of the items above are off, let me know and I’ll update the recap. Otherwise, expect Marissa's numbers tomorrow.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today — latency/throughput checklist

Hi Alex — following up with the micro-benchmark we discussed. I ran a short, targeted suite against the model configuration we usually recommend for this class of workload (FP16, kv-cache enabled, standard attention kernels). Key numbers below reflect 290-token average generation on an A100-class instance with Redwood serving runtime defaults. Attached is the raw CSV with run-by-run numbers.

Benchmark summary (single-shard numbers, no external batching):
- Concurrency 1 (no batching): P50 = 115 ms / P90 = 320 ms / P99 = 950 ms; tokens/sec (generation) ≈ 620 t/s
- Concurrency 4 (internal continuous batching, batch size tuned 1-8): P50 = 140 ms / P90 = 360 ms / P99 = 980 ms; tokens/sec ≈ 2,200 t/s
- Concurrency 8 (aggressive batching): P50 = 210 ms / P90 = 560 ms / P99 = 1,450 ms; tokens/sec ≈ 3,900 t/s

Observations & recommendations:
- For your 95% < 1800 ms SLO the single-shard numbers are already in range at concurrency <=8; P99 heads toward the higher end when we push batching aggressively.
- If RetailCo traffic is bursty (short spikes to 200 req/s), a multi-shard Dedicated pool or autoscaling warmup reduces P99 risk.
- Suggested starting config for PoC: 2 x A100 shards with continuous batching (max batch 8), pre-warmed pool and short 60s cold-start SLA — this should give ~4k-6k t/s effective capacity and P99 comfortably under 1.2 s for your generation shape.

Caveats:
- These runs exclude network overhead and retailco-specific pre/post-processing. If your infra adds 150-300 ms, we should account for that in the SLO.
- If you plan to quantize aggressively (8-bit), expect some additional variance on P99 — we can test that in the PoC.

Attachments: retailco-bench-sheet.csv

Happy to walk through the CSV live — Karthik, if it helps I can do a 20-minute call with Alex to step through the numbers next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Checking in — are latency numbers still a go / any change in priority?

Alex — just circling back since it’s been a week since Marissa sent the benchmark CSV. Wanted to check two quick things: 

1) Priority: is the fraud-assistant PoC still on the Q4 roadmap? If timing shifted, I can re-scope the pilot to a smaller pilot (single route + synthetic traffic) and reprioritize costs.
2) Questions on the numbers: did anything in Marissa's runs look off relative to what you expected? If you want, we can run the same profile with your pre/post-processing steps (adds realism to the P99 calc).

Proposed low-effort next step if you’re still interested: 10-day sandbox (no infra commit) where we mirror one production route and run 2k synthetic requests/day to validate P95/P99 under your exact pre/post-processing. That gets to a reliable cost estimate and lets you see real tails without a long integration.

If now isn’t the right time, totally fine — please let me know and I’ll close the loop. If you are interested, what time next week works for a quick 15-min sync?

Thanks for the time,
